chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a slave who was emancipated as a Sa'ibah (unconditionally freed slave). He said: 'He has a guardian of his choice, and upon the one who becomes his guardian is his liability (for his debts/crimes), and for him is his inheritance.' I said: 'So if he remains without a guardian until he dies?' He said: 'His wealth is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

key_terms.جَرِيرَة: Liability or debt (often referring to financial obligations or blood money)
key_terms.سَائِبَة: An unconditionally freed slave who chooses their own guardian

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for an unconditionally freed slave (Sa'ibah) regarding guardianship and inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the legal mechanism of 'takhallus' (emancipation) for a Sa'ibah, emphasizing the autonomy of the freed slave to select a patron who assumes both financial liability (jarirah) and inheritance rights. The ruling reflects the early Islamic administrative practice where, in the absence of a designated guardian, the state treasury (Bayt al-Mal) acts as the final custodian of the estate, ensuring no property remains ownerless. This principle underscores the Shia juristic view of the Imam or Caliph as the ultimate guardian for those without kin or chosen patrons.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a slave who emancipated a slave unconditionally. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His guardian would be whoever he so like, and upon the one who is his guardian would be his crimes, and for him would be his inheritance’. I said, ‘So if it remains such until he dies (without a guardian)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His wealth would be made to be in the public treasury of the Muslims’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from [his father] from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd from Yunus from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the slave who is freed in the manner of Sa’ibah (unconditionally freed slave). He (the Imam) said, ‘He is free to choose a guardian whoever he likes to bail out his liabilities due to crime and then inherit his legacy. ’I then asked, ‘What happens if he remains quiet until he dies?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘His legacy is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.’”
